check_description: Re-derive every block SMILES a second time, from the Figure 2a/3a drawings and the SI chemical names, without consulting the first draft, then compare each resulting molecular formula against the block mass solved independently from product mass balance in Tables S1/S2.
what_it_would_catch: A mis-drawn or mis-counted chain, a wrong amine, a wrong linker identity, a one-carbon error anywhere.
method: RDKit formula and average MW from the redrawn SMILES, versus the block mass obtained by solving product = amine + n x (linker + thiol - leaving group) against the paper's reported product MWs.
expected: Agreement within rounding (<0.1 Da) for every block that any reported product constrains.
observed: All 8 amine cores, all 8 linkers and 6 of 8 tails agree to <=0.06 Da. Examples: L5 EMCS C14H16N2O6 308.29 vs 308.23 solved from T3A-L5-C10; L1 SMCC C16H18N2O6 334.33 vs 334.33 solved from T3A-L1-2C10; T3A C9H24N4 188.32 vs 188.3 solved from 70/113/T3A L8 series; 2C10 C19H40S 300.60 vs 300.59 solved across L1, L6, L7 and L8 independently.
note: 2C11 and 2C12 are not constrained by any reported product mass and rest on the drawing alone.

check_description: Degree of substitution against the paper's own arithmetic.
what_it_would_catch: A systematic error replicated across every member of the library.
method: Compare DS = number of primary amines against the Table S1/S2 feed ratios and against the stated library sizes.
expected: 8 amines x 8 BLs x 5 thiols = 320; 1 amine x 8 BLs x 3 thiols = 24; total 344 as claimed in the abstract.
observed: 320 + 24 = 344, matching the abstract exactly. Feed ratios track primary-amine count exactly: 1:1.05:1.1 for 70/75/80/400 (1 primary NH2), 1:2.05:2.1 for 113 (2), 1:3.05:3.1 for 110/T3A (3). Mass balance confirms 1 arm on 70 and 400, 2 on 113, 3 on 110 and T3A.
note: The one-arm-per-primary-amine rule is confirmed on 5 of the 8 amine cores; 80 and 114 have no representative product, and 75 only via L1/L2 rows.

check_description: Whether L2 is a maleimide linker at all, and therefore whether its products are thiosuccinimides.
what_it_would_catch: The entire L2 sub-library (40 lipids in library 1, 3 in library 2) carrying the wrong bond type and the wrong mass.
method: Close the mass balance for 75-L2-C6, 113-L2-C8 and 110-L2-C10 under two competing hypotheses: maleimide thiol-Michael (lose NHS only) versus 2-pyridyldithio disulfide exchange (lose NHS and 2-pyridinethione).
expected: One hypothesis closes to rounding; the other fails by a large, constant margin.
observed: Disulfide-exchange closes at 320.55 vs 320.6, 582.00 vs 582.0 and 927.60 vs 927.6. The maleimide hypothesis is 111.16 Da per arm too heavy, i.e. 333 Da off for the three-arm product. The Figure 2a drawing independently shows a 2-pyridyldithio group, not a maleimide.
note: Finding, not an error in my draft: the paper itself calls all 344 members thiosuccinimide lipids, but L2-derived lipids are disulfides. These are reducible in the cytosol, which is a different structure-activity class, and L2 is also the only linker that releases a second byproduct.

check_description: The L4 versus L5 assignment.
what_it_would_catch: Two linkers interchanged across a whole sub-library, a 28 Da per arm error invisible to any single-row check.
method: Test every Table S1 L4 and L5 row against both GMBS (280.24) and EMCS (308.29), and cross-check against the Figure 2a drawings, the Results text and Table S2.
expected: L4 rows match GMBS, L5 rows match EMCS.
observed: All three rows labelled L4 match EMCS, not GMBS: 399.59/740.08/1122.64 calculated vs 399.6/740.1/1122.6 reported (GMBS would give 371.54/683.97/1038.48). Two of the three rows labelled L5 match GMBS: 427.65/796.18 vs 427.7/796.2 (EMCS would give 455.70/852.29). Only T3A-L5-C10 matches EMCS at 1290.96 vs 1290.9.
note: Table S1 has the L4 and L5 masses interchanged. Three independent sources outvote it: the Figure 2a drawings show 3 CH2 for L4 and 5 CH2 for L5; the Results call L5 the 'n-5CH2 alkyl chain linker'; Table S2 gives L4 = 280.23 and L5 = 307.83 solved from T3A-L4-2C10 and T3A-L5-2C10. T3A-L5-C10 is additionally confirmed by the Figure S12 LC-MS [M+H]+ of 1292. CSV 1 follows the drawing, the text and Table S2.

check_description: Duplicate and mislabelled rows in Table S1.
what_it_would_catch: A linker silently missing from the representative set, and a double-counted compound.
method: Test the three anomalous rows in the second L6 block against both L6 and L7.
expected: 24 distinct representative lipids across 8 linkers.
observed: Row 19 (labelled 400-L6-C6, 516.7) matches 400-L7-C6 at 516.74, not L6 at 472.69. Row 21 (labelled T3A-L6-C6, 1260.7) matches T3A-L7-C6 at 1260.71, not L6 at 1128.56. Row 20 (113-L6-C6, 744.0) is an exact duplicate of row 17. So Table S1 carries no row under the L7 label at all, and lists 22 distinct compounds, not 24.
note: Does not change any block structure or condition: L7 is independently fixed by its SI chemical name, its drawing and Table S2.

check_description: Internal consistency of the L3 rows.
what_it_would_catch: A wrong linker length for L3.
method: Mass balance on all three L3 rows in Table S1.
expected: All three consistent with AMAS (252.18).
observed: 70-L3-C6 agrees within 1.3 Da and T3A-L3-C6 within 0.01 Da, but 113-L3-C6 is reported as 613.8 against 627.86 calculated, short by 14.06 Da, exactly one CH2.
note: Isolated transcription error in one row. The L3 = AMAS assignment stands on the other two rows, the Table S2 row (251.76 solved) and the drawing.

check_description: Whether the 2Cn tail token means what it looks like.
what_it_would_catch: A 14 Da per tail error, 42 Da per six-tail lipid, applied to all 24 members of library 2.
method: Compare the 2C10 mass solved from four independent linkers against a literal 'two C10 chains' reading (C20, 314.62) and against the generic CH3-(CH2)n-2 structure drawn in Figure 3b.
expected: One reading matches the solved mass.
observed: Solved mass is 300.59 from each of L1, L6, L7 and L8 separately, i.e. C19H40S. The literal C20 reading is 14.03 Da per tail too heavy. The Figure 3b generic drawing gives 2n-1 carbons, so 2C10 = C19, and direct vertex counts on Figure 3a confirm 9 carbons per branch for 2C10, 10 for 2C11 and 11 for 2C12.
note: Finding: for 2Cn each arm is n carbons only if the shared S-bearing methine is counted in both arms. Enumerating these tails as 2n-carbon chains would corrupt every library 2 structure.

check_description: Regiochemistry of acylation on the two amines that carry a secondary NH (400 and 114).
what_it_would_catch: An arm placed on the wrong nitrogen, which molecular formula and HRMS cannot distinguish.
method: Look for a stated route, a drawn product, or feed stoichiometry that pins the site.
expected: Either direct evidence, or an empty cell plus a note.
observed: For 400 the 1:1.05:1.1 feed ratio plus mass balance on two separate products fix exactly one arm, so only the primary amine is acylated. For 114 there is no Table S1 row, no product mass, no drawn product and no text statement; nothing in the paper pins whether the central NH reacts.
note: 114 is carried at n_reactive_sites = 2 by analogy with 400 only. If the central NH did react, every 114-derived lipid in library 1 (40 of 320) would carry three arms rather than two.

check_description: Stereochemistry created or carried by the chemistry.
what_it_would_catch: Structures enumerated as single stereoisomers when they are mixtures.
method: Inspect the bond-forming step and the drawn reagents for stereocentres.
expected: Either stereochemistry specified, or recorded as unspecified.
observed: Thiol-Michael addition to the symmetric maleimide creates a stereocentre at succinimide C3, so every arm is racemic and the two- and three-arm lipids are diastereomer mixtures; the paper neither draws nor mentions this. Separately, L1 (SMCC) is cyclohexane-1,4-disubstituted, a cis/trans pair, drawn without stereochemistry and with no vendor or purity stated.
note: Maleimide symmetry means there is no C3-versus-C4 regiochemical choice to get wrong, only stereochemistry. SMILES in CSV 1 are written without stereodescriptors at these centres, deliberately.

check_description: In vivo luciferase dose, caption against Methods.
what_it_would_catch: Two different experiments merged into one condition row, or a dose off by ten-fold.
method: Read the Methods and every in vivo luciferase figure caption separately.
expected: A single consistent dose, or distinct doses attributable to distinct experiments.
observed: The Methods and the Figure 5 caption both say 1 mg/kg. The Figure S14c and Figure S18d captions both say 0.1 mg/kg. These are genuinely different experiments, not a contradiction.
note: Recorded as separate conditions: C12 at 1 mg/kg, C13 and C15 at 0.1 mg/kg. A reader taking the Methods dose as global would mis-assign C13 and C15 by ten-fold.

check_description: Identity of the PEG lipid.
what_it_would_catch: The wrong PEG lipid propagated into every formulation row.
method: Compare the SI materials list against the main text, Methods and every formulation caption.
expected: One PEG lipid named consistently.
observed: Every formulation in the main text, Methods, Figure S11, Figure S13b and Figure S18 specifies DMG-PEG 2000. The SI materials list instead names a phosphoethanolamine-N-[methoxy(poly(ethylene glycol))-2000] from Sigma-Aldrich, which is a DSPE-PEG2000-type lipid, not a DMG-PEG. The paper never reconciles the two.
note: peg_lipid_identity is recorded as DMG-PEG 2000 throughout, since that is what every formulation statement says, with the conflict flagged on block PG1. SMILES is left empty regardless because PEG2000 is polydisperse.

check_description: Arithmetic of the printed formulation ratios.
what_it_would_catch: A transcription error in a formulation that would be silently renormalised downstream.
method: Sum each printed four-component molar ratio.
expected: Each set sums to 100.
note: F5 (50/10/48.5/1.5) is the single offender, summing to 110 rather than 100. It is recorded verbatim in C10 and deliberately not renormalised; which of the four numbers is wrong cannot be determined from the paper.

check_description: Hit-rate denominators against library sizes.
what_it_would_catch: A hit rate computed over the wrong group size.
method: Divide each library by the grouping used in each hit-rate panel.
expected: Caption n matches the group size.
observed: Figure 2d states n = 40 per amine-core group, which equals 8 BLs x 5 thiols, correct for library 1. The Figure 3 caption states n = 8 for both panel 3d and panel 3e, but grouping 24 lipids by BL gives 3 per group; only the per-tail grouping in 3d gives 8.
note: Affects the hit-rate values, which are out of scope here, not the conditions themselves.

check_description: The tail set named in the Results against the tail set drawn and tabulated.
what_it_would_catch: A tail that does not exist being attributed to a library.
method: Compare the Figure 2f discussion with Figure 2a and Table S1.
expected: The same five tails.
observed: Figure 2a draws C6, C8, C10, C12 and C14 for library 1 and Table S1 uses C6, C8, C10 and C14. The Results nevertheless say lipids with a C10 tail outperformed 'those with C11 or C12 tails'. Library 1 contains no C11; the C11 and C12 labels belong to library 2's branched 2C11 and 2C12 set.
note: CSV 1 carries the five linear tails that are drawn, not the ones named in that sentence.

check_description: Whether each commercial benchmark is named precisely enough to pin a structure.
what_it_would_catch: A benchmark lipid resolved to the wrong molecule.
method: Check each trade name for ambiguity, citation and vendor, and check whether a mass test could detect a swap.
expected: Each benchmark unambiguously resolvable.
observed: DLin-MC3-DMA (C43H79NO2, 642.11) and ALC-0315 (C48H95NO5, 766.29) are unambiguous. 'Lipid 5' and 'SM102' are given as bare tokens with no citation, vendor or structure; both resolve to Moderna lipids that are constitutional isomers of each other (both C44H87NO5, 710.18), so a swap between them would be invisible to any mass check. '18PA' is named only inside the phrase 'SORT LNP' and its formulation ratio is given nowhere in the paper.
note: CL3, CL4 and HL4 are carried at med confidence for this reason, and the SORT comparator formulation is left empty in C12 and C16 rather than assumed from the cited SORT literature.

check_description: Core in vitro and in vivo conditions, Results against Methods, read separately.
what_it_would_catch: A condition silently taken from the wrong place.
method: Read the Methods in full, then each figure caption, and compare field by field.
expected: Agreement, or both readings recorded.
observed: Agreement on HeLa, 1e4 cells per well in 96-well black plates, 20 ng mFluc per well, 24 h, pipette mixing ~300 times, citrate pH 4.0, lipid:mRNA 20:1, 35/16/46.5/2.5, dialysis 1x PBS 20K MWCO 3 h, luciferin 200 uL at 15 mg/mL i.p. imaged 3 min later, female C57BL/6J 6-8 weeks from Beijing Vital River. Ai9 mouse sex, age and supplier are stated nowhere.
note: Ai9 model_sex and model_age are left empty in C16 rather than carried over from the C57BL/6J protocol.

check_description: What the 20:1 weight ratio is a ratio of.
what_it_would_catch: Ionizable-lipid-to-mRNA confused with total-lipid-to-mRNA, roughly a 3x difference.
method: Compare the two places the ratio is stated.
expected: One definition.
observed: The Results say 'a lipid/mRNA weight ratio of 20:1'; the Methods say 'LNP/mRNA weight ratio of 20:1'. Neither defines which lipid mass is meant, and the paper never gives a total-lipid or ionizable-lipid mass.
note: Recorded verbatim as 20:1 in IL_to_nucleic_acid_wt_ratio with this caveat. Treating it as ionizable-lipid-to-mRNA would be an assumption the paper does not support.

check_description: Provenance of the T3A amine core.
what_it_would_catch: A core used in 64 of 344 lipids resting on an unsourced identification.
method: Search the SI materials list and the main text for T3A's chemical name, vendor, purity or CAS.
expected: Named like the other seven amines.
observed: T3A appears nowhere in the SI materials list, which does name all seven other amine cores with vendor and purity, including the closely related 110. No chemical name, vendor, purity or CAS is given for T3A anywhere in the paper.
note: Identity (tris(3-aminopropyl)amine) is taken from the Figure 2a and 3a drawings and is corroborated by mass balance on 24 products in Tables S1 and S2, so the structure is secure even though the sourcing is not.

check_description: Particle size, DLS against TEM.
what_it_would_catch: Two different size values merged into one cell.
method: Compare Figure S11b with the Figure S18f TEM statement.
expected: One size, or two attributable to different methods.
observed: Figure S11b gives 72.4 +/- 0.5 nm for T3A-L5-2C10 by DLS; the Results report 'an average size of approximately 50 nm' from TEM of 'bare' T3A-L5-2C10 LNPs. Different methods, and 'bare' may mean cargo-free. The paper does not reconcile them.
note: particle_size_nm carries the DLS value, which is the one tied to the characterised formulation; the TEM figure is noted in C15.

check_description: Whether the reaction is operationally one step or two.
what_it_would_catch: reaction_description misstating the protocol.
method: Compare the title and abstract with the Methods and Figure 1a.
expected: Consistent description.
observed: The title and abstract call it a 'one-pot, two-step' three-component reaction, but the Methods combine amine, BL and alkyl-thiol in a single vial and heat once at 80 C for 4 h, and Figure 1a draws all three components converging on a single arrow labelled BL-3CR. 'Two-step' appears to describe the two bond-forming events, not two operations.
note: reaction_description in CSV 2 follows the Methods, which is the operational account, and names the two bond-forming events explicitly rather than repeating the phrase 'two-step'.
